mappings.note: Asks which quality the Hira-Moti bond shows (ekta aur sahyog). LO-2 is the friendship/mutual-cooperation outcome; not LO-1, which wants the whole story's saar and central message.
Refusal to accept Gaya's place because being sold felt like apmaan -- an act of protest against ill-treatment, so LO-3 (atyachar and vidroh episodes), not LO-2's friendship thread.
Why they broke the rope and went home: the rebellion episode itself. LO-3 rather than C-3.1-LO-1, which wants the freedom-symbol evaluation, not the event's motive.
Moti's aakrosh at Gaya's beating = swabhiman; response to atyachar, so LO-3. Not LO-2: the trigger is the oppression, not the friendship.
Purpose of the mook-bhasha device. LO-2 is exactly the animals' mute language; LO-1 would be Premchand's wider style features.
Hira-Moti as symbols in the freedom struggle -- the symbolic-tale evaluation of LO-1 under C-3.1, not plain comprehension under C-1.1.
Why they refused to work for the new master: non-cooperation as protest, LO-3. Not LO-1, which asks for the story's overall message.
Three episodes proving they were abhinn mitra -- LO-2 asks for exactly those friendship episodes.

Compare the malkin's conduct with the little girl's. No LO of this chapter covers character comparison (LO-1/2/3 are saar, friendship, atyachar), so the analysis/evaluation competency C-3.1 is cited at competency level.
'If you were that girl, how would you help?' -- a reasoned personal position, C-2.1. Not C-2.2: nothing is composed in a set form (no diary, samvad or letter).
Agree/disagree that fear holds people back, with evidence from story plus own experience -- reasoned opinion, C-2.1.
Agree/disagree on dhaul-dhappa as a mark of close friendship, justified from experience. Opinion, so C-2.1, not C-1.1-LO-2, which wants episodes from the text.
Take Hira's side or Moti's on striking a fallen enemy, and defend it -- argued viewpoint, C-2.1. Not C-4.2: the item asks the student's position, not the value the text carries.
Recount facing a hardship together with a friend -- own experience, reasoned expression, C-2.1.
Find the opening's signals about character, time, language and events -- craft/style observation, LO-1 under C-1.2. Not LO-2, which is only about mook-bhasha.
Match story sentences to freedom-struggle statements: the allegorical reading, C-3.1-LO-1.
How the kanjihaus confinement shows both justice and injustice -- the atyachar episode and its meaning, LO-3.
Which legal rights would you demand for the bullocks -- a reasoned stand on a social issue, C-2.1.

Write a complaint letter in Hira and Moti's own voice. LO-1 is the write-in-their-viewpoint outcome; the form here is a patra rather than a sansmaran/diary, but the first-person bullock voice is the distinguishing demand. Not LO-2, which is the Jhuri-Gaya samvad.
Which acts the bullocks never did ('apna dharm') -- their moral code, part of the story's central message, LO-1. Item 21 asks about the Indian values behind the same lines and is mapped differently.

Hira's kahavat-like sayings ('gire hue bairi par sing na chalana', 'aurat jaat par sing chalana mana hai') and the Indian values they point to. C-4.3-LO-2 is precisely kahavatein showing social conduct; C-4.2 for the cultural values themselves.
How you want classmates with different needs to treat you, and they you -- reasoned view on a social issue, C-2.1.
Imagine how the two talked in mook-bhasha -- the mute-language outcome, C-1.2-LO-2.
When do you yourself communicate without words -- still the mook-bhasha idea extended to the reader, so LO-2 rather than C-2.1.
Have you ever lost your way and how did you find it -- own experience, C-2.1. The bullocks losing their way is only the prompt.

Write a new ending. Creative composition, so C-2.2 at competency level; not C-3.1-LO-2, which evaluates whether the existing ending is justified rather than replacing it, and not C-2.2-LO-1/LO-2, whose forms (diary, Jhuri-Gaya samvad) are not what is asked.
Chitrakatha: supply dialogue and linking sentences for four panels. Creative writing, C-2.2 at competency level -- LO-2 is specifically the Jhuri-Gaya samvad, which this is not.
Pick five new words, guess their meanings, then check a dictionary -- the word-list-and-use outcome C-4.1-LO-2, not LO-1, which is muhavare.
Muhavara 'danton pasina aana' -- give the meaning and use it in a new sentence. C-4.1-LO-1 is the idiom outcome; the stem lost its instruction line but the answer confirms the task.
Muhavara 'dil kaanpna' -- meaning plus own sentence, C-4.1-LO-1.
Muhavara 'jal uthna' -- meaning plus own sentence, C-4.1-LO-1, not a comprehension outcome.
Muhavara 'dil mein aithkar rah jana' -- meaning plus own sentence, C-4.1-LO-1.
Muhavara 'khabar lena' -- meaning plus own sentence, C-4.1-LO-1.
Two muhavare, 'ji todkar kaam karna' and 'gam kha jana' -- meanings plus own sentences, C-4.1-LO-1.
Muhavara 'eint ka jawab patthar se dena' -- meaning plus own sentence, C-4.1-LO-1.
Muhavara 'nau-do-gyarah hona' -- meaning plus own sentence, C-4.1-LO-1.

The word 'bail' across Eighth Schedule languages, plus write the sentence in your mother tongue. This is Indian linguistic diversity, so C-4.3 (language's role in identity) at competency level and its goal CG-4; C-4.3-LO-1 is narrower -- rural life and its boli in this story only.
Who wrote 'Do Bailon ki Katha'. Authorship recall, which no LO of this chapter states; cited at competency level under C-1.1 (reading literary works).
Premchand's real name. Biographical recall, no LO covers it, so C-1.1 at competency level.
Which animal is held most witless -- recall from the opening passage, part of grasping the text's content, LO-1.
What is always on the donkey's face (sthayi vishad) -- content recall, LO-1.
Whom Premchand compares the donkey to (rishis and munis). The item turns on the author's comparison, a style device, so C-1.2-LO-1 rather than plain recall under C-1.1-LO-1.
What made Japan count among civilised nations, per the text -- content recall, LO-1.
The bullocks' names -- basic content recall, LO-1.
Their breed (pachhain) -- content recall, LO-1; not C-4.1-LO-2, since no word list or use is asked for.
Each tried to take more of the load -- the cooperation detail, LO-2, not generic recall.
Where they were first sent (to Gaya's) -- content recall, LO-1.
Assertion-reason on refusing the naand at Gaya's because the home was lost -- protest at ill-treatment, LO-3.
They broke the paghe at night and left -- the rebellion event, LO-3.
Where Jhuri found them at dawn (at the charni) -- content recall, LO-1.
Their legs were caked to the knee with mud -- content recall, LO-1.
Which of three statements about the homecoming are true -- content recall, LO-1.
The wife's order that they get only dry bhusa -- punishment, so the atyachar strand LO-3 rather than neutral recall.
What Gaya yoked them to the second time (a cart) -- content recall, LO-1.
Moti tried to tip the cart into the ditch -- an act of resistance, LO-3.
After 'teaching them a lesson' Gaya gave only dry bhusa -- the ill-treatment sequence, LO-3.
Which girl fed them rotis (Bhairo's daughter) -- content recall, LO-1.
What the text says of the girl's mother -- content recall, LO-1.
Assertion-reason on the orphan girl's atmiyata with the bullocks -- comprehension of the text's compassion thread, LO-1; LO-2 is reserved for the two bullocks' own bond.
Whose anger broke loose when Hira's nose was beaten (Moti's) -- the atyachar-and-revolt sequence, LO-3.
Hira stops Moti: taking a beating is not our kind's dharm -- a statement inside the resistance episode, LO-3.
Moti's plan to chew the rope first -- the escape/rebellion method, LO-3.
The girl's warning as she loosed them -- content recall, LO-1.
Why they stood still after being freed (suspicion would fall on the orphan girl) -- their consideration for her, part of the story's message, LO-1; LO-2 covers only the bond between the two bullocks.

Statement III -- Hira turned back and let himself be caught rather than leave Moti -- makes this the friendship outcome LO-2. Note: this item's options and answer key are corrupted (they belong to another question).
In whose form Hira believed God had saved them (the little girl) -- content recall, LO-1.
What they saw on the road with the bearded man (a contented herd) -- content recall, LO-1.
Statements about the auction and Moti chasing the bearded buyer off -- the resistance sequence, LO-3.
Effect on the bullocks when the familiar road appeared (fatigue vanished) -- content recall, LO-1.
Moti used his horns when the buyer seized the ropes -- an act of revolt, LO-3.
Hira to Moti: I feared you would kill him. Counsel between the two friends, LO-2, rather than the oppression strand LO-3.
Moti's answer that they are treated as nothing 'because we are so meek' -- the theme of oppression borne by the gentle, LO-3.
What Jhuri's wife did at the end (kissed their foreheads) -- content recall of the ending, LO-1; not C-3.1-LO-2, which asks the student to judge that ending.
Their physical state after a week in the kanjihaus (ribs showing) -- the consequence of atyachar, LO-3.
Why buyers walked away disheartened -- no one buys near-dead bullocks; the outcome of their ill-treatment, LO-3.

Why Premchand calls the donkey most witless while praising its qualities -- evaluating an apparent contradiction (irony). No LO fits: C-3.1-LO-1 is the freedom allegory and LO-2 the ending, so the competency C-3.1 is cited.
How the bhaichara between them came about -- the friendship outcome LO-2.
How they resisted being taken to Gaya's -- the protest episode, LO-3.
Why they would not touch the naand at Gaya's -- refusal as protest, LO-3.
How they escaped Gaya's the first time and got home -- the rebellion events in order, LO-3.

Why the wife called them 'namakharaam' and Jhuri's reply. The item turns on a sambodhan used for animals and what it reveals of social attitude -- exactly C-4.3-LO-2, not plain recall under C-1.1-LO-1.
Why the orphan girl felt a kinship the household did not -- the story's compassion message, LO-1.
Why Hira said fleeing is cowardice when Moti faced the saand -- standing together, LO-2.
Why Hira broke the kanjihaus wall despite the risk of beating -- the revolt episode, LO-3.
Moti failed to free Hira's rope and then stayed rather than escape -- the clearest friendship episode, LO-2.

Contrast Jhuri's wife with the little girl and the effect on the bullocks. Character comparison, which no LO of this chapter names, so C-3.1 at competency level (same treatment as the earlier malkin/girl comparison).
Why mook-bhasha recurs and its literary and emotional value -- C-1.2-LO-2.
Their thoughts while being led away after the auction -- despair under oppression, LO-3.
Episodes proving that struggle is sometimes necessary -- the atyachar-and-vidroh events, LO-3.
Compare Hira's and Moti's characters. Unlike the malkin/girl comparisons, this is the pair LO-2 names, and it asks what Premchand conveys through them.
Full allegorical reading against the freedom movement -- C-3.1-LO-1.
What Jhuri, Gaya and the wife reveal of peasant life -- rural life and its cultural identity, C-4.3-LO-1, rather than a comprehension LO.
Analyse swatantrata, swabhiman and mitrata together: LO-1 for the central message, C-3.1-LO-1 for the freedom strand specifically.
Place the story in the Panchatantra tradition and say what is new. That is the reason-it-is-a-symbolic-tale outcome, C-3.1-LO-1, not a style outcome under C-1.2.
Detailed analysis of the whole kanjihaus episode -- the atyachar and revolt sequence, LO-3.
